citations.quote: Internalization, order preferencing, and internal order crossing all arrange trades away from organized markets.
a broker commits to route his orders to a specific dealer, and the dealer commits to execute them at the best quoted price in the market or even to improve systematically upon these prices.
Dealers expose themselves to well-informed traders and to large traders when they offer firm quotes that any trader can take.
If he does internalize, he will refrain from bidding in the main market; otherwise, he would be competing against himself on the internalized portion.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Internalization (in-house dealer fills), preferencing (routing to a paying dealer at NBBO), and internal crossing all arrange trades away from organized markets, diverting benign flow from public price discovery and raising cream-skimming and best-execution concerns.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Internalization, Preferencing, and Crossing Networks
